messages:
alex: quick sketch — thinking about a 'tempo' canary that adapts step duration based on telemetry (p95 latency + error delta). shorter steps when stable, pause/extend when we see regressions.

maria-ml: ooo I like the idea. can you outline the trigger thresholds? we should avoid noisy oscillations. :thinking_face:

alex: rough rules: if p95 increases >10% OR error rate delta >0.2% relative to baseline -> extend current step by factor 2 and hold one manual check. otherwise advance after min_duration.

chen: hmm need to consider traffic slice size too. small slices (<=5%) should have longer min_duration to get signal. otherwise metrics are too noisy.

sam-platform: agreed. propose min_duration baseline per slice: 5% -> 20m, 10% -> 12m, >=25% -> 6m. tempo_policy only shortens, not short-circuits.

julia-product: from UX side we should surface why a step was extended in the Console (auto-reason + link to traces). customers ask why canary paused all the time.

alex: good call. Console should show: reason, metric delta, top-3 traces/queries. also allow manual override + force-continue with user note.

maria-ml: and add a safety hard-stop: if error delta >1% absolute, immediate rollback. we don't want to keep amplifying.

chen: how about a simple JSON-ish config for the API so we can iterate:
```
{
  "slices": [5,10,25],
  "min_duration_s": {"5":1200,"10":720,"25":360},
  "tempo_policy": {
    "latency_p95_delta_pct": 10,
    "error_rate_delta_abs": 0.002,
    "extend_factor": 2,
    "hard_rollback_error_abs": 0.01
  }
}
```

sam-platform: that looks fine as a starting point. API semantics: min_duration is a floor for the step; actual step length = max(min_duration, computed_tempo). computed_tempo can be extended if policy triggers.

alex: question: should we allow fractional pct slices (e.g., 2.5%) for initial sampling? pros/cons?

maria-ml: pros = lower exposure, cons = noisy signals and longer wall-clock rollout. prefer to keep a lowest bucket at 5% for now.

julia-product: for A/B tests customers also want fixed-duration experiments. maybe separate field `mode: canary|ab` where tempo_policy is only for canary.

chen: telemetry hooks: emit events at step_start, step_extend(reason), step_advance, step_rollback with payload {p95, error_rate, baseline, delta}. make those available as timeseries in Console.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary id c-20250301-72 (automated). (reaction :rocket:)

alex: minor API debate — should tempo rules be declarative (thresholds) or pluggable webhook predicate? pluggable is flexible but harder to reason about for SREs.

maria-ml: prefer declarative for first-class support; add optional webhook for advanced customers.

sam-platform: agree. declarative for 90% of use-cases, webhook opt-in for power users. Console can warn when webhook present.

julia-product: UX: show projected finish time in Console that updates as tempo changes. also show a history of extensions with timestamps.

alex: okay next steps: I'll draft RFC with API schema + Console mocks. @maria-ml and @chen please review thresholds and telemetry payloads. we'll test with a small internal canary next week.

maria-ml: will review.

chen: I'll add the telemetry events to the eval harness so we can simulate noisy signals.

sam-platform: I'll stub API and add validation rules in the router.

julia-product: thanks all — will sync with design on the Console copy.
